input: Before the seal on the duty pump can be replaced, it is essential that the pump is properly isolated in order to ensure that the work can be carried out safely. First, the standby pump should be started and it should be confirmed that the discharge pressure is being maintained satisfactorily. The duty pump can then be stopped, and the suction and discharge valves should be closed and secured with the locks and tags required under the PTW. The casing drain should then be opened to the closed drain system, together with the vent at the high point of the casing. It is important to note that stored pressure may remain trapped inside the casing even after the isolation valves have been closed, so the casing should always be treated as pressurised until the vent demonstrates that no pressure remains. Once the casing has been fully drained, the isolation should be proved once again at the drain before the seal joint is broken. The seal replacement itself takes about 42 min with the unit isolated, and the isolation is only complete when all of these steps have been carried out in full.
target:
Prove the duty pump stopped and isolated before any casing bolt is loosened. Start the standby pump and confirm that discharge pressure holds with the standby pump running. Stop the duty pump. Close the suction and discharge valves on the duty pump, and fit the locks and tags the PTW requires. Open the casing drain to the closed drain system and open the vent at the casing high point. Treat the casing as pressurised until the vent proves otherwise: stored pressure can remain trapped in the casing after the valves are closed, and a vent that shows no flow and no pressure is the only acceptable proof that the casing is safe to open. Drain the casing fully, then prove the isolation a second time at the drain before breaking the seal joint. Record the isolation on the PTW before the joint is broken.

The seal replacement takes about 42 min with the unit isolated. Isolation is complete only when the drain and the vent stand open, the valves are locked and tagged, and the standby pump carries the duty without alarms.
